intro: Slim, thin and skinny can describe the same person, but only one of them is a compliment. Today you'll learn to hear the feeling behind a word (its connotation), to swap vague words like good and big for precise ones, and to choose words that fit a reference letter, a complaint or a news report. Warm-up: think of a time someone used a word about you that was technically true but felt wrong.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: in b2-formal-informal-vocab the learner chose between formal and informal partners (get → receive / obtain, find out → discover, help → assist) for different readers. New here: words at the SAME level of formality that carry a different feeling. Connotation (konotasi, 'rasa' atau 'nilai' sebuah kata) = the positive, neutral or negative feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning (denotation). Indonesian bridge: langsing (positive) / kurus (neutral) / kurus kering (negative); hemat / pelit; tegas / keras kepala; percaya diri / sombong; ingin tahu / kepo. The core message: a dictionary or Google Translate often gives a list of 'synonyms' without the feeling, so learners pick the first one and accidentally insult someone.

Synonym sets (positive / neutral / negative): slim / thin / skinny (skinny often negative = too thin; informal; but 'skinny jeans' and some young speakers use it neutrally); thrifty, economical (careful with money; economical also for things: an economical car) / stingy, mean (pelit; 'mean' = stingy in British English, but usually 'unkind' in American English); firm, determined (tegas, gigih) / stubborn, obstinate (keras kepala; obstinate is more formal and even more negative); confident / arrogant; curious / nosy (kepo; informal); assertive (states needs clearly and respectfully) / aggressive, pushy (in business, 'aggressive targets / marketing' can be approving: be honest about this); relaxed, laid-back / lazy; inexpensive, affordable / cheap (cheap is fine for prices in everyday speech, e.g. cheap flights, but about objects it often suggests low quality: cheap plastic); childlike (innocent, full of wonder: positive) / childish (behaves badly like a child: negative); famous / notorious (famous for something bad); young (neutral) / youthful (positive: looks or feels young) / immature (negative: behaves younger than they should). The node's common errors: 'Your grandmother looks skinny and beautiful' → slim; 'Our manager is stubborn, which really helps the team' → firm. Trap: economic (about the economy) ≠ economical (hemat), from Indonesian 'ekonomis'.

Precise words (objective precise-words): Indonesian 'bagus' and English 'good' cover almost everything, so reports full of good / bad / big / thing / get sound vague. Ask WHAT is good about it: effective (works, gets results: efektif), reliable (works every time, can be trusted: andal), valuable (very useful or important: berharga), beneficial (good for someone's health or situation: bermanfaat), high-quality (well made: berkualitas tinggi). bad → harmful (to health, the environment), unreliable, poor (quality, service, performance), damaging (to a reputation, relationship). big → substantial (amount, investment), significant (important change: a significant increase), extensive (covers a wide area: extensive damage, extensive experience). thing → issue (problem to deal with), factor (one cause or influence in a decision), aspect (one part or side of something), item (on a list or agenda). get → obtain (with effort: a visa, permission), receive (an email, a payment), gain (experience, skills, an advantage). Collocations to stress: highly effective (common error 'The new method is very good' → highly effective), a significant increase, a substantial investment, extensive experience, gain experience. Be honest: 'good' is fine in conversation; precision matters most in reports, reviews, applications.

Matching tone (objective match-word-to-tone): reference letter → warm, positive words (reliable, determined, confident, a quick learner); complaint → firm but polite (I was disappointed that …, I would like a full refund; no insults, and not so soft that it sounds optional: 'no worries if not'); news report → neutral (said, demonstrators, the government; not loaded words like mob, heroes, regime); performance review → constructive (an area to improve, could be more thorough, needs to check the figures; not lazy / careless). Euphemisms (eufemisme: a softer, polite word for something unpleasant): let go (= dismissed, fired: diberhentikan), pre-owned (= second-hand: bekas), budget-friendly (= cheap: ramah di kantong), passed away (= died). Say honestly that euphemisms are polite but can also hide the real meaning (a company says 'let go' to sound kind; a reader should notice what really happened).

At C1 many word choices are about style, so accept reasonable alternatives (determined / firm, substantial / significant / considerable, effective / successful) and only mark clear cases wrong: a negative word where the writer clearly means praise, a vague word when a precise one was asked for, or a word whose tone clashes with the text type. Explain the feeling of the word rather than calling it 'wrong English': 'stubborn is correct English, but it criticises'. Also note gently that in English-speaking workplaces comments on someone's body or weight are sensitive, even positive ones, while in Indonesia 'kamu kurusan ya' is common small talk.

Limits: A0–B2 grammar plus b2-formal-informal-vocab. No inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive, impersonal passives or advanced participle clauses in examples; 'were let go' is an ordinary passive (known from B2). Don't teach rare literary words (svelte, emaciated, parsimonious, penny-pinching as a test item); if the learner uses one correctly, accept it and say it's rare. Contexts: reference letters, hotel and restaurant reviews, complaints to suppliers, HR announcements, performance reviews, news about Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya and Yogyakarta, prices in rupiah.

keyPoints.title: Same meaning, different feeling
keyPoints.explanation: Connotation is the feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning: positive, neutral or negative. Many synonyms sit on a line: slim / thin / skinny, thrifty / stingy, firm, determined / stubborn, confident / arrogant, curious / nosy, assertive / aggressive, pushy, relaxed / lazy, affordable / cheap (cheap can suggest low quality), childlike / childish, famous / notorious, youthful / young / immature. Choose the word that says what you really feel: praise with the positive one, criticise with the negative one.

examples.en: My sister is slim and very fit.
examples.id: Kakak perempuanku langsing dan sangat bugar.

examples.en: Pak Hasan is firm with deadlines, so the team always delivers on time.
examples.id: Pak Hasan tegas soal tenggat, jadi timnya selalu menyelesaikan tepat waktu.

examples.en: He's so stingy that he never pays for coffee.
examples.id: Dia pelit sekali sampai tidak pernah membayar kopi.

id.title: Arti sama, rasa berbeda
id.explanation: Konotasi adalah 'rasa' sebuah kata di luar arti kamusnya: positif, netral atau negatif. Banyak sinonim berada di satu garis: slim / thin / skinny (langsing / kurus / kurus kering), thrifty / stingy (hemat / pelit), firm, determined / stubborn (tegas, gigih / keras kepala), confident / arrogant (percaya diri / sombong), curious / nosy (ingin tahu / kepo), assertive / aggressive, pushy (tegas dan sopan / agresif, memaksa), relaxed / lazy (santai / malas), affordable / cheap (terjangkau / murah, bisa berarti murahan), childlike / childish (polos seperti anak / kekanak-kanakan), famous / notorious (terkenal / terkenal karena hal buruk), youthful / young / immature (awet muda / muda / belum dewasa). Pilih kata yang sesuai dengan maksudmu: untuk memuji pakai yang positif, untuk mengkritik pakai yang negatif.

keyPoints.title: Precise words instead of vague ones
keyPoints.explanation: Ask what exactly is good, bad or big. good → effective (it works), reliable (it works every time), valuable (very useful), beneficial (good for someone), high-quality (well made). bad → harmful, unreliable, poor, damaging. big → substantial (an amount), significant (an important change), extensive (a wide area). thing → issue, factor, aspect, item. get → obtain (with effort), receive, gain (experience, skills). Learn them with their partners: highly effective, a significant increase, extensive experience.

examples.en: The new booking app is highly effective: waiting times fell by half.
examples.id: Aplikasi pemesanan yang baru sangat efektif: waktu tunggu turun separuhnya.

examples.en: Plastic waste is harmful to marine life.
examples.id: Sampah plastik berbahaya bagi kehidupan laut.

examples.en: She gained valuable experience at an NGO in Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Dia memperoleh pengalaman berharga di sebuah LSM di Yogyakarta.

id.title: Kata yang presisi sebagai ganti kata yang samar
id.explanation: Tanyakan apa tepatnya yang bagus, buruk atau besar. good → effective (berhasil, efektif), reliable (andal, selalu bisa diandalkan), valuable (berharga), beneficial (bermanfaat bagi seseorang), high-quality (berkualitas tinggi). bad → harmful (berbahaya, merugikan), unreliable (tidak andal), poor (buruk, kurang baik), damaging (merusak). big → substantial (jumlahnya cukup besar), significant (perubahan yang penting/berarti), extensive (luas). thing → issue (masalah), factor (faktor), aspect (aspek), item (butir, barang). get → obtain (memperoleh, dengan usaha), receive (menerima), gain (mendapat pengalaman, keterampilan). Hafalkan bersama pasangannya: highly effective, a significant increase, extensive experience.

keyPoints.title: Match the word to the tone of the text
keyPoints.explanation: Every text has a purpose, and the words must fit it. A reference letter praises: reliable, determined, confident. A complaint is firm but polite: I was disappointed that …, I would like a refund (no insults). A news report is neutral: said, demonstrators, the government (not mob or heroes). A performance review is constructive: could be more thorough, an area to improve (not lazy). Euphemisms are softer, polite words: let go (= dismissed), pre-owned (= second-hand), budget-friendly (= cheap). They're polite, but they can also hide the real meaning.

examples.en: Rina is reliable, determined and a quick learner.
examples.id: Rina bisa diandalkan, gigih, dan cepat belajar.

examples.en: I was disappointed that my order arrived two weeks late.
examples.id: Saya kecewa pesanan saya datang dua minggu terlambat.

examples.en: Thirty staff were let go after the merger.
examples.id: Tiga puluh karyawan diberhentikan setelah merger.

id.title: Sesuaikan kata dengan nada teksnya
id.explanation: Setiap teks punya tujuan, dan kata-katanya harus cocok. Surat rekomendasi memuji: reliable, determined, confident. Surat keluhan tegas tapi sopan: I was disappointed that …, I would like a refund (tanpa hinaan). Berita bersifat netral: said, demonstrators, the government (bukan mob atau heroes). Penilaian kinerja bersifat membangun: could be more thorough, an area to improve (bukan lazy). Eufemisme adalah kata yang lebih halus dan sopan: let go (= dipecat, diberhentikan), pre-owned (= bekas), budget-friendly (= murah, ramah di kantong). Kata-kata ini sopan, tapi juga bisa menyembunyikan arti sebenarnya.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the positive word (confident / arrogant): Sari spoke in a calm, ___ voice during the pitch, and the investors trusted her.
guidedPractice.hint: The investors trusted her: that's praise, so choose the word with a positive feeling (percaya diri, not sombong).

guidedPractice.prompt: Positive, neutral or negative? 'Pak Budi is so pushy in meetings.'
guidedPractice.hint: pushy = memaksa, mendesak orang lain terus-menerus. Is that a compliment?

guidedPractice.prompt: Replace 'bad for' with one more precise adjective + 'to': 'Air pollution is bad for children's lungs.' → Air pollution is ___ to children's lungs.
guidedPractice.hint: A word that means 'causes harm' (berbahaya, merugikan).

guidedPractice.prompt: Replace 'get' with a more precise word: 'Our interns get useful experience in project management.'
guidedPractice.hint: The verb that usually goes with experience, skills and knowledge.

guidedPractice.prompt: A shop selling second-hand designer bags wants a softer, more attractive word for its website. Complete with one word: '___-owned bags in excellent condition'.
guidedPractice.hint: A polite euphemism for second-hand (bekas), often used for cars and luxury goods.

independentPractice.prompt: Which word fits a neutral news report better: 'regime' or 'government'?
independentPractice.hint: 'regime' suggests an unfair or undemocratic government: it takes a side.

independentPractice.prompt: Replace 'big' with a more precise word: 'The company made a big investment in solar panels for its factory in Surabaya.'
independentPractice.hint: For an amount of money, a word like 'substantial' sounds more precise and professional.

independentPractice.prompt: 'relaxed' is the positive word. Write its negative partner (malas).
independentPractice.hint: Someone who doesn't want to work or make an effort.

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani is writing a reference letter for her assistant. Choose the word with a POSITIVE connotation from this list: stubborn, determined, obstinate. 'Dewi is ___: once she has set a goal, she keeps working until she achieves it.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: determined (gigih, bertekad kuat: praise, which a reference letter needs). 'stubborn' = 0 and 'obstinate' = 0 (keras kepala: both criticise, so they would hurt Dewi's application). A word from outside the list with the right feeling ('persistent', 'firm') = 70 (positive, but the task asked for a word from the list). Small spelling error that keeps the word clear ('determind') = 80.

assessment.prompt: Complete this restaurant review with the word from the list that suggests LOW QUALITY: affordable, inexpensive, cheap. 'The food was tasty, but the plastic chairs felt ___ and one of them broke while I was eating.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: cheap (here it means murahan: badly made, low quality, which matches the broken chair). 'affordable' = 0 and 'inexpensive' = 0 (they only describe a low price, often positively, and say nothing about poor quality). A word outside the list with the right meaning ('flimsy', 'low-quality') = 70 (right idea, but the task asked for a word from the list).

assessment.prompt: Choose from: childlike, childish. 'Hiding a colleague's laptop as a joke during an important client meeting was ___ and unprofessional.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: childish (kekanak-kanakan: behaving badly, like a child; negative, which matches 'unprofessional'). 'childlike' = 0 (it's positive: innocent and full of wonder, e.g. childlike curiosity). Spelling error that keeps the word clear ('childsh') = 80.

assessment.prompt: Make this report sentence more precise. Write the ONE word that completes 'highly ___' (= it got the result it was meant to get): 'The anti-dengue campaign in Surabaya was very good: dengue cases fell by 40% in six months.' → The campaign was highly ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: effective (efektif: it did what it was meant to do, and 'highly effective' is the natural partner); 'successful' is also accepted. 'beneficial' = 60 (good for people, but it doesn't say the campaign achieved its goal). 'reliable' = 30 (it means working every time, not getting a result). 'good' / 'very good' = 0 (the vague word the task asked to replace). 'efficient' = 50 (it means doing something without wasting time or money, a different idea).

assessment.prompt: Replace 'thing' with a more precise word: 'Price was the most important thing in our decision to choose a supplier in Bandung; delivery time mattered less.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: factor (faktor: one of the influences on a decision); 'consideration' and 'criterion' are also accepted. 'aspect' = 60 (one side of something, less natural for a reason in a decision). 'issue' = 40 (it suggests a problem to deal with). 'item' = 20 (a thing on a list). 'point' = 70 (understandable, but less precise).

assessment.prompt: This is from a neutral news report. Choose the word from the list that doesn't take a side: troublemakers, demonstrators, heroes. 'About 2,000 ___ gathered outside the parliament building in Jakarta on Monday to oppose the new tax.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: demonstrators (pengunjuk rasa: a neutral description of people at a protest). 'troublemakers' = 0 (negative: it criticises them). 'heroes' = 0 (positive: it praises them). A news report should do neither. A neutral word from outside the list ('protesters', 'people') = 80 (the right tone, but the task asked for a word from the list).

assessment.prompt: The HR department is writing a kind, polite announcement to all staff. Complete it with ONE word to make the polite phrase that means 'dismissed': 'Sadly, twelve employees at our Surabaya branch were ___ go last month because of falling sales.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: let ('were let go' = were dismissed, diberhentikan: the polite euphemism HR uses). 'allowed to go' = 50 (it means they were given permission to leave, not dismissed). 'made to go' = 30 (harsh, not polite). 'fired' / 'sacked' in place of the phrase = 20 (correct meaning, but direct and informal, the opposite of the tone asked for).

material.title: Connotation: the feeling behind a word

id.title: Konotasi: rasa di balik sebuah kata

blocks.text:
At B2 you chose between **formal and informal** words for different readers (get → receive, find out → discover). Today the words are at the same level of formality, but they **feel** different.

Every word has a dictionary meaning (its **denotation**). Many words also carry a feeling: **positive**, **neutral** or **negative**. That feeling is the word's **connotation**.

You already know this from Indonesian. *Langsing*, *kurus* and *kurus kering* can describe the same body, but only *langsing* is a compliment. *Hemat* praises someone who is careful with money; *pelit* criticises the same habit. *Tegas* is a strength in a manager; *keras kepala* is a problem. English works the same way:
- **slim** (langsing) / **thin** (kurus) / **skinny** (kurus kering)
- **thrifty** (hemat) / **stingy** (pelit)
- **firm** (tegas) / **stubborn** (keras kepala)

id.text:
Di B2 kamu memilih antara kata **formal dan informal** untuk pembaca yang berbeda (get → receive, find out → discover). Hari ini kata-katanya sama tingkat formalitasnya, tapi **rasanya** berbeda.

Setiap kata punya arti kamus (disebut **denotasi**). Banyak kata juga membawa 'rasa' atau nilai: **positif**, **netral** atau **negatif**. Rasa itulah yang disebut **konotasi** kata tersebut.

Kamu sebenarnya sudah mengenalnya dari bahasa Indonesia. *Langsing*, *kurus* dan *kurus kering* bisa menggambarkan tubuh yang sama, tapi hanya *langsing* yang terdengar sebagai pujian. *Hemat* memuji orang yang berhati-hati dengan uang; *pelit* mengkritik kebiasaan yang sama. *Tegas* adalah kelebihan seorang manajer; *keras kepala* adalah masalah. Bahasa Inggris juga begitu:
- **slim** (langsing) / **thin** (kurus) / **skinny** (kurus kering)
- **thrifty** (hemat) / **stingy** (pelit)
- **firm** (tegas) / **stubborn** (keras kepala)

blocks.text:
**The dictionary trap.** A dictionary or Google Translate often gives a list of 'synonyms' with no feeling attached: *kurus → thin, skinny, slim*. If you take the first one, you might insult someone without knowing it. When you look up a word, check an English–English learner's dictionary: it often marks words as **approving** (positive) or **disapproving** (negative), and its examples show the feeling.

A cultural note: in Indonesia, *'Kamu kurusan ya!'* is normal small talk. In English-speaking workplaces, comments on someone's body or weight are sensitive, even kind ones, so many people avoid them completely.

id.text:
**Jebakan kamus.** Kamus atau Google Translate sering memberi daftar 'sinonim' tanpa rasanya: *kurus → thin, skinny, slim*. Kalau kamu ambil yang pertama, kamu bisa menyinggung orang tanpa sadar. Saat mencari kata, cek kamus pelajar Inggris–Inggris: kamus seperti itu sering memberi label **approving** (positif) atau **disapproving** (negatif), dan contoh kalimatnya menunjukkan rasanya.

Catatan budaya: di Indonesia, *'Kamu kurusan ya!'* adalah basa-basi biasa. Di tempat kerja berbahasa Inggris, komentar tentang tubuh atau berat badan seseorang itu sensitif, bahkan yang bernada baik, jadi banyak orang menghindarinya sama sekali.

blocks.prompt: Which word has a NEGATIVE connotation?
blocks.explain: stingy = pelit: it criticises someone for not wanting to spend or share money. thrifty (hemat) and economical (hemat, irit) describe the same habit in a positive way.

id.prompt: Kata mana yang punya konotasi NEGATIF?
id.explain: stingy = pelit: kata ini mengkritik orang yang tidak mau mengeluarkan atau berbagi uang. thrifty (hemat) dan economical (hemat, irit) menggambarkan kebiasaan yang sama dengan cara yang positif.

material.title: Positive, neutral, negative: synonym sets to know

id.title: Positif, netral, negatif: kelompok sinonim yang perlu kamu tahu

blocks.text:
Read each line from **positive** to **negative**:
- **slim** (langsing) → **thin** (kurus) → **skinny** (kurus kering, terlalu kurus)
- **thrifty / economical** (hemat) → **stingy / mean** (pelit)
- **firm / determined** (tegas / gigih) → **stubborn / obstinate** (keras kepala; obstinate is more formal and even stronger)
- **confident** (percaya diri) → **arrogant** (sombong)
- **curious** (ingin tahu) → **nosy** (kepo, suka ikut campur)
- **assertive** (tegas tapi sopan) → **aggressive / pushy** (agresif / suka memaksa)
- **relaxed / laid-back** (santai) → **lazy** (malas)
- **affordable / inexpensive** (terjangkau) → **cheap** (murah, often murahan)
- **childlike** (polos seperti anak) → **childish** (kekanak-kanakan)
- **famous** (terkenal) → **notorious** (terkenal karena hal buruk)
- **youthful** (awet muda, penuh semangat muda) → **young** (muda: neutral) → **immature** (belum dewasa)

id.text:
Baca setiap baris dari **positif** ke **negatif**:
- **slim** (langsing) → **thin** (kurus) → **skinny** (kurus kering, terlalu kurus)
- **thrifty / economical** (hemat) → **stingy / mean** (pelit)
- **firm / determined** (tegas / gigih) → **stubborn / obstinate** (keras kepala; obstinate lebih formal dan lebih kuat lagi)
- **confident** (percaya diri) → **arrogant** (sombong)
- **curious** (ingin tahu) → **nosy** (kepo, suka ikut campur)
- **assertive** (tegas tapi sopan) → **aggressive / pushy** (agresif / suka memaksa)
- **relaxed / laid-back** (santai) → **lazy** (malas)
- **affordable / inexpensive** (terjangkau) → **cheap** (murah, sering berarti murahan)
- **childlike** (polos seperti anak) → **childish** (kekanak-kanakan)
- **famous** (terkenal) → **notorious** (terkenal karena hal buruk)
- **youthful** (awet muda, penuh semangat muda) → **young** (muda: netral) → **immature** (belum dewasa)

rows.en: Our CEO is confident, but never arrogant.
rows.id: CEO kami percaya diri, tapi tidak pernah sombong.

rows.en: My neighbour is so nosy: she asks everyone how much they earn.
rows.id: Tetanggaku kepo sekali: dia bertanya ke semua orang berapa gaji mereka.
rows.note: nosy is informal; British English also spells it nosey

id.note: nosy itu informal; dalam bahasa Inggris British juga ditulis nosey

rows.en: A good salesperson is assertive, not pushy.
rows.id: Tenaga penjual yang baik tegas dan jelas, bukan suka memaksa.

rows.en: Even at 70, Pak Hasan has a youthful energy.
rows.id: Meski sudah 70 tahun, Pak Hasan punya semangat yang awet muda.
rows.note: youthful = positive; young is just neutral

rows.en: We're looking for an affordable hotel near Malioboro.
rows.id: Kami mencari hotel yang terjangkau di dekat Malioboro.
rows.note: affordable = a fair price, no hint of low quality

id.note: affordable = harga yang wajar, tanpa kesan kualitas rendah

blocks.text:
**Words that change with the context — be careful:**
- **cheap** is fine for prices in everyday speech (*cheap flights to Bali*). About **things**, it often means badly made: *a cheap plastic toy* (murahan).
- **mean** = stingy in **British** English (*He's too mean to share his snacks*), but in **American** English it usually means **unkind** (jahat, tidak baik hati).
- **aggressive** is usually negative about people, but in business it can sound approving: *aggressive growth targets* (ambisius).
- **skinny** is negative about people, but neutral in fashion: *skinny jeans*.
- **economical** = hemat (*an economical car*). **economic** = about the economy (*economic growth*). The Indonesian word *ekonomis* means **economical**, not *economic*.

id.text:
**Kata yang rasanya berubah sesuai konteks — hati-hati:**
- **cheap** wajar untuk harga dalam percakapan sehari-hari (*cheap flights to Bali*). Untuk **barang**, sering berarti dibuat asal-asalan: *a cheap plastic toy* (murahan).
- **mean** = pelit dalam bahasa Inggris **British** (*He's too mean to share his snacks*), tapi dalam bahasa Inggris **Amerika** biasanya berarti **tidak baik hati** (jahat).
- **aggressive** biasanya negatif untuk orang, tapi dalam bisnis bisa terdengar positif: *aggressive growth targets* (ambisius).
- **skinny** negatif untuk orang, tapi netral di dunia fashion: *skinny jeans*.
- **economical** = hemat (*an economical car*). **economic** = berkaitan dengan ekonomi (*economic growth*). Kata Indonesia *ekonomis* artinya **economical**, bukan *economic*.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Drivers call it 'the road of death': that part of the highway is ___ for serious accidents.
blocks.explain: notorious = known for something bad, which matches serious accidents. famous is for things people admire or enjoy (Bandung is famous for its cool weather).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Drivers call it 'the road of death': that part of the highway is ___ for serious accidents.
id.explain: notorious = terkenal karena hal buruk, cocok dengan kecelakaan serius. famous dipakai untuk hal yang dikagumi atau disukai orang (Bandung is famous for its cool weather).

material.title: Precise words for good, bad, big, thing and get

id.title: Kata yang presisi untuk good, bad, big, thing dan get

blocks.text:
In Indonesian, *bagus* can describe almost anything. English **good** is the same, so a report full of *good*, *bad*, *big* and *thing* sounds vague. Ask: **what exactly** is good about it?

**good →**
- **effective** (efektif): it works, it gets the result: *a highly effective treatment*
- **reliable** (andal): it works every time, you can trust it: *a reliable supplier*
- **valuable** (berharga): very useful or important: *valuable feedback*
- **beneficial** (bermanfaat): good for someone's health or situation: *beneficial for older people*
- **high-quality** (berkualitas tinggi): well made: *high-quality materials*

**bad →** **harmful** (berbahaya: *harmful to health*), **unreliable** (tidak andal), **poor** (buruk: *poor service*), **damaging** (merusak: *damaging to the company's reputation*)

**big →** **substantial** (an amount: *a substantial investment*), **significant** (an important change: *a significant increase*), **extensive** (a wide area or range: *extensive damage, extensive experience*)

**thing →** **issue** (a problem to deal with), **factor** (one reason or influence), **aspect** (one part or side of something), **item** (one thing on a list or agenda)

**get →** **obtain** (with effort: *obtain a visa*), **receive** (*receive an email*), **gain** (*gain experience, gain skills*)

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *bagus* bisa dipakai untuk hampir semua hal. **good** dalam bahasa Inggris juga begitu, jadi laporan yang penuh *good*, *bad*, *big* dan *thing* terdengar samar. Tanyakan: **apa tepatnya** yang bagus?

**good →**
- **effective** (efektif): berhasil, mencapai hasilnya: *a highly effective treatment*
- **reliable** (andal): selalu berfungsi, bisa dipercaya: *a reliable supplier*
- **valuable** (berharga): sangat berguna atau penting: *valuable feedback*
- **beneficial** (bermanfaat): baik untuk kesehatan atau keadaan seseorang: *beneficial for older people*
- **high-quality** (berkualitas tinggi): dibuat dengan baik: *high-quality materials*

**bad →** **harmful** (berbahaya: *harmful to health*), **unreliable** (tidak andal), **poor** (buruk: *poor service*), **damaging** (merusak: *damaging to the company's reputation*)

**big →** **substantial** (jumlah: *a substantial investment*), **significant** (perubahan yang penting: *a significant increase*), **extensive** (wilayah atau cakupan yang luas: *extensive damage, extensive experience*)

**thing →** **issue** (masalah yang perlu ditangani), **factor** (satu alasan atau pengaruh), **aspect** (satu bagian atau sisi dari sesuatu), **item** (satu butir di daftar atau agenda)

**get →** **obtain** (dengan usaha: *obtain a visa*), **receive** (*receive an email*), **gain** (*gain experience, gain skills*)

rows.en: The new booking app is highly effective: waiting times fell by half.
rows.id: Aplikasi pemesanan yang baru sangat efektif: waktu tunggu turun separuhnya.
rows.note: highly effective, not 'very good': it says what is good

id.note: highly effective, bukan 'very good': menyebut apa yang bagus

rows.en: Poor lighting in the warehouse caused several accidents.
rows.id: Pencahayaan yang buruk di gudang menyebabkan beberapa kecelakaan.

rows.en: The earthquake caused extensive damage in the district.
rows.id: Gempa itu menyebabkan kerusakan yang luas di kabupaten tersebut.

rows.en: Staff turnover is a serious issue for many startups.
rows.id: Pergantian karyawan adalah masalah serius bagi banyak startup.

rows.en: You need to obtain a permit before you build a second floor.
rows.id: Kamu harus memperoleh izin sebelum membangun lantai dua.

blocks.text:
**Learn the partner words (collocations).** Precise words sound natural with their usual partners: **highly** effective, **a significant** increase, **a substantial** amount, **extensive** experience, **gain** experience, **obtain** permission. Don't write *'a big damage'*: say **extensive damage** or **serious damage**.

And be honest with yourself: **good** isn't wrong. In conversation it's perfectly natural. Precision matters most in reports, reviews, job applications and anything people will read carefully.

id.text:
**Hafalkan kata pasangannya (kolokasi).** Kata yang presisi terdengar alami bersama pasangan biasanya: **highly** effective, **a significant** increase, **a substantial** amount, **extensive** experience, **gain** experience, **obtain** permission. Jangan menulis *'a big damage'*: katakan **extensive damage** atau **serious damage**.

Dan jujur saja: **good** itu tidak salah. Dalam percakapan, kata itu wajar sekali. Ketepatan kata paling penting di laporan, ulasan, lamaran kerja, dan semua tulisan yang akan dibaca dengan teliti.

blocks.prompt: Which word is the most precise replacement for 'good' here? 'Regular walking is good for older people's hearts.'
blocks.explain: beneficial = good for someone's health or situation (bermanfaat), followed by for. reliable is for something that works every time; high-quality is for something well made.

id.prompt: Kata mana yang paling presisi untuk mengganti 'good' di sini? 'Regular walking is good for older people's hearts.'
id.explain: beneficial = baik untuk kesehatan atau keadaan seseorang (bermanfaat), diikuti for. reliable untuk sesuatu yang selalu berfungsi; high-quality untuk sesuatu yang dibuat dengan baik.

material.title: Match the tone: letters, complaints, news, reviews and euphemisms

id.title: Sesuaikan nada: surat, keluhan, berita, penilaian dan eufemisme

blocks.text:
**Tone** (nada) is the attitude a text shows: warm, angry, neutral, polite. Before you write, ask what the text is **for**:
- **A reference letter** (surat rekomendasi) praises: choose positive words: *reliable, determined, confident, a quick learner*.
- **A complaint** (keluhan) is **firm but polite**: say clearly what went wrong and what you want, with no insults: *I was disappointed that …*, *I would like a full refund.* Not too soft either: *'No worries if not!'* makes your request sound optional.
- **A news report** is **neutral**: it doesn't take sides: *said*, *demonstrators*, *the government* (not *mob*, *heroes* or *regime*, which praise or criticise).
- **A performance review** (penilaian kinerja) is **constructive** (membangun): it names the problem and how to improve, without labels like *lazy* or *careless*: *Her reports could be more thorough.*

**Euphemisms** (eufemisme) are softer, polite words for something unpleasant or uncomfortable:
- **let go** = dismissed, fired (diberhentikan)
- **pre-owned** = second-hand (bekas)
- **budget-friendly** = cheap (ramah di kantong)
- **passed away** = died (meninggal dunia)

id.text:
**Nada** (tone) adalah sikap yang ditunjukkan sebuah teks: hangat, marah, netral, sopan. Sebelum menulis, tanyakan teks itu **untuk apa**:
- **Surat rekomendasi** (reference letter) memuji: pilih kata yang positif: *reliable, determined, confident, a quick learner*.
- **Keluhan** (complaint) itu **tegas tapi sopan**: sebutkan dengan jelas apa yang salah dan apa yang kamu minta, tanpa hinaan: *I was disappointed that …*, *I would like a full refund.* Jangan juga terlalu lunak: *'No worries if not!'* membuat permintaanmu terdengar tidak wajib.
- **Berita** bersifat **netral**: tidak memihak: *said*, *demonstrators*, *the government* (bukan *mob*, *heroes* atau *regime*, yang memuji atau mengkritik).
- **Penilaian kinerja** (performance review) bersifat **membangun** (constructive): menyebut masalahnya dan cara memperbaikinya, tanpa label seperti *lazy* atau *careless*: *Her reports could be more thorough.*

**Eufemisme** (euphemism) adalah kata yang lebih halus dan sopan untuk hal yang tidak menyenangkan atau tidak nyaman:
- **let go** = dismissed, fired (diberhentikan, dipecat)
- **pre-owned** = second-hand (bekas)
- **budget-friendly** = cheap (ramah di kantong)
- **passed away** = died (meninggal dunia)

rows.en: During her internship, Rina was reliable, determined and a quick learner.
rows.id: Selama magang, Rina bisa diandalkan, gigih, dan cepat belajar.

rows.en: I was disappointed that my order arrived two weeks late, and I would like a partial refund.
rows.id: Saya kecewa pesanan saya datang dua minggu terlambat, dan saya ingin pengembalian dana sebagian.

rows.en: The minister said the new rules would start in January.
rows.id: Menteri mengatakan aturan baru akan mulai berlaku pada bulan Januari.

rows.en: Dimas needs to check the figures more carefully before he sends a report.
rows.id: Dimas perlu memeriksa angka-angkanya dengan lebih teliti sebelum mengirim laporan.

rows.en: The showroom in Bandung sells pre-owned cars with a one-year warranty.
rows.id: Showroom di Bandung itu menjual mobil bekas dengan garansi satu tahun.

blocks.text: **Euphemisms are polite, and sometimes they hide things.** Saying *passed away* to a grieving colleague is kind. But companies also use soft words so that bad news sounds less bad: *thirty staff were let go* sounds gentler than *thirty staff lost their jobs*, but it's the same event. Use euphemisms to be polite; when you **read** them, notice what really happened.

id.text: **Eufemisme itu sopan, dan kadang menyembunyikan sesuatu.** Mengatakan *passed away* kepada rekan yang sedang berduka itu baik hati. Tapi perusahaan juga memakai kata yang halus supaya kabar buruk terdengar tidak terlalu buruk: *thirty staff were let go* terdengar lebih lembut daripada *thirty staff lost their jobs*, padahal kejadiannya sama. Pakai eufemisme untuk bersikap sopan; saat kamu **membacanya**, perhatikan apa yang sebenarnya terjadi.

blocks.prompt: Dimas's reports often contain small mistakes in the figures. Which sentence fits a constructive performance review?
options: Dimas is lazy and careless with his reports.
Dimas's reports would be stronger if he checked the figures more carefully.
Dimas's reports are perfect. No comments!
blocks.explain: A constructive review names the problem and the way to improve it. 'lazy and careless' only attacks him; 'perfect' isn't true and doesn't help him improve.

id.prompt: Laporan Dimas sering berisi kesalahan kecil pada angka-angkanya. Kalimat mana yang cocok untuk penilaian kinerja yang membangun?
id.explain: Penilaian yang membangun menyebut masalahnya dan cara memperbaikinya. 'lazy and careless' hanya menyerang orangnya; 'perfect' tidak benar dan tidak membantunya berkembang.

resources.title: Shrewd or cunning, modern or newfangled? Connotation in English
resources.note: A blog post by Liz Walter on approving and disapproving words: slim / thin / skinny, shrewd / cunning, modern / newfangled and more, and how a learner's dictionary shows connotation. It includes some rare words (svelte, emaciated) that you don't need to learn.

id.intro: Slim, thin dan skinny bisa menggambarkan orang yang sama, tapi hanya satu yang terdengar sebagai pujian. Hari ini kamu belajar merasakan 'rasa' di balik sebuah kata (konotasinya), mengganti kata yang samar seperti good dan big dengan kata yang presisi, dan memilih kata yang cocok untuk surat rekomendasi, surat keluhan atau berita. Pemanasan: ingat saat seseorang memakai kata tentang dirimu yang secara arti benar, tapi rasanya kurang enak.
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana saya tahu sebuah kata itu positif atau negatif?
Apakah eufemisme seperti 'let go' itu tidak jujur?

assessment.cn-1: Bu Ani sedang menulis surat rekomendasi untuk asistennya. Pilih kata dengan konotasi POSITIF dari daftar ini: stubborn, determined, obstinate. 'Dewi is ___: once she has set a goal, she keeps working until she achieves it.'
assessment.cn-2: Lengkapi ulasan restoran ini dengan kata dari daftar yang memberi kesan KUALITAS RENDAH (murahan): affordable, inexpensive, cheap. 'The food was tasty, but the plastic chairs felt ___ and one of them broke while I was eating.'
assessment.cn-3: Pilih dari: childlike, childish. 'Hiding a colleague's laptop as a joke during an important client meeting was ___ and unprofessional.'
assessment.cn-4: Buat kalimat laporan ini lebih presisi. Tulis SATU kata bahasa Inggris yang melengkapi 'highly ___' (= mencapai hasil yang diharapkan): 'The anti-dengue campaign in Surabaya was very good: dengue cases fell by 40% in six months.' → The campaign was highly ___.
assessment.cn-5: Ganti 'thing' dengan kata bahasa Inggris yang lebih presisi: 'Price was the most important thing in our decision to choose a supplier in Bandung; delivery time mattered less.'
assessment.cn-6: Ini dari sebuah berita yang netral. Pilih kata dari daftar yang tidak memihak: troublemakers, demonstrators, heroes. 'About 2,000 ___ gathered outside the parliament building in Jakarta on Monday to oppose the new tax.'
assessment.cn-7: Bagian HR sedang menulis pengumuman yang halus dan sopan untuk semua karyawan. Lengkapi dengan SATU kata bahasa Inggris supaya menjadi frasa sopan yang berarti 'diberhentikan': 'Sadly, twelve employees at our Surabaya branch were ___ go last month because of falling sales.'
